title: Effect of Oxygen Affinity of Liposome-Encapsulated Hemoglobin on Cerebral Ischemia and Reperfusion as Detected by Positron Emission Tomography in Nonhuman Primates.
abstract: We tested a hypothesis that liposome-encapsulated hemoglobin (LEH) with high oxygen (O<sub>2</sub> ) affinity (h-LEH, P<sub>50</sub> O<sub>2</sub>  = 10 mm Hg) may work better than LEH with low O<sub>2</sub> affinity (l-LEH, P<sub>50</sub> O<sub>2</sub>  = 40 mm Hg) in cerebral ischemia and reperfusion injury using positron emission tomography (PET) in primates undergoing middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion and reperfusion. Cerebral blood flow (CBF), O<sub>2</sub> extract fraction (OEF), and cerebral metabolic rate of O<sub>2</sub> (CMRO<sub>2</sub> ) were successively determined by PET before ischemia, at 2 h of ischemia, immediately after reperfusion, and 3 h after reperfusion. Five minutes after MCA occlusion, 10 mL/kg of h-LEH (n = 6) was intravenously infused and compared with the results from previous data of monkeys treated with l-LEH (n = 6), empty liposome (n = 4), or saline (n = 8) as control. After the series of PET studies, the integrated area of cerebral infarction was determined histologically in 12 coronal brain slices. There was no significant difference in CBF, OEF, or CMRO<sub>2</sub> up to 2 h of ischemia. A high CBF with a low OEF tended to be suppressed after reperfusion in LEH-treated monkeys. Three hours after reperfusion, the area of mild CMRO<sub>2</sub> reduction (down to -30%) decreased (P < 0.05) and the area of mild CMRO<sub>2</sub> increase (up to 30%) expanded in LEH-treated monkeys (P < 0.05) regardless of O<sub>2</sub> affinity with no difference in the area of moderate-to-severe reduction (<-30%) or increase (<+30%) in CMRO<sub>2</sub> compared to animals treated with empty liposome or saline. Distribution of CMRO<sub>2</sub> reduction and histological damages showed that LEH mainly protected the cerebral cortex rather than basal ganglia where neuronal dendritic processes were severely lost. There was little difference between the animals treated with l-LEH or h-LEH both at 10 mL/kg or between treatment with empty liposome or saline. In conclusion, LEH was effective regardless of O<sub>2</sub> affinity in preserving CMRO<sub>2</sub> and in reducing the area of histological damage in the cerebral cortex, but not in basal ganglia, shortly after occlusion/reperfusion of MCA in monkey.
